newsitem.title: USA: U.S., EU raise subsidy issues in aviation talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., EU raise subsidy issues in aviation talks.

text.p: Trade negotiators for the United States and European Union on Friday discussed concerns about implementation of a 1992 agreement limiting direct and indirect subsidies to civil aviation industries.

A spokesman for the U.S. Trade Representative said that during the two days of talks U.S. negotiators expressed concern about sales promotions subsidies while the Europeans talked about indirect U.S. subsidies for civil aviation through military contracts. The 1992 trade agreement sets limits for direct and indirect subsidies to civil aviation industries.
Neither side brought up the proposed merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, which the European Commission is scheduled to consider on July 23, the spokesman said.

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told reporters on Friday that she hoped the Europeans would consider the the Boeing merger solely on the basis of competition and not allow political considerations to enter the decision.
"We have been concerned about some of the rhetoric coming out of Europe," she said.

The European Union has been critical of the proposed merger and said it should be blocked unless changed. Officials have said they were concerned that the merger would add to Boeing's dominant position in global markets.
